narrative.headline: Watch the transmission first on the 2020 Explorer
narrative.summary: Owners filed 1,138 complaints to NHTSA. The power train (transmission and drivetrain) dominates by far at 439 reports (39%) - more than the next two categories combined. Electrical and engine problems follow, with a handful of fires tied to each. Before you buy, get a thorough test drive and a transmission check.

issues.title: Power Train
issues.blurb: The single biggest complaint area: 439 reports (39% of all). Owners describe rough shifting and drivetrain failures, sometimes mid-drive. Linked to 6 crashes and 2 injuries. Test-drive hard and watch for jerky or hesitant shifts.

issues.title: Electrical System
issues.blurb: Second most common: 175 reports (15%). Includes glitches and unexpected behavior, with 4 fires, 3 crashes, and 2 injuries reported. Check that all electronics work normally and look for any warning lights.

issues.title: Engine
issues.blurb: 109 reports (10%), including early failures and stalling. Tied to 4 fires and 2 crashes. Listen for unusual noises and confirm the engine runs smoothly cold and warm.

issues.title: Back Over Prevention
issues.blurb: 104 reports (9%), often a rearview camera that blanks out. This one carries 8 crashes - the most of any category here - and 1 injury. Confirm the backup camera shows a clear, steady image every time.

issues.title: Service Brakes
issues.blurb: 80 reports (7%), but the highest injury count here at 6, plus 4 crashes - some owners describe reduced stopping power. Test the brakes carefully and have a mechanic inspect them before buying.
